sentences.text: The present petition has been filed under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (corresponding to Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023), seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.585/2015 dated 23.09.2015 registered at Police Station Sarni, District Betul (M.P.), for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467 and 468 of Indian Penal Code, as well as all consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

2. Brief facts giving rise to the present petition are that as per the prosecution, a written complaint was submitted by the complainant (respondent No.2 herein), namely the Principal, Government Industrial Training Institute, Betul before the concerned police station on 23.09.2015.

It NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25633 2 MCRC-18039-2017 was alleged that the present petitioner, who was functioning as the In- charge/Principal of Radhakrishnan and Chaitanya I.T.I.,
was operating the institute under three different names within the same building, in contravention of applicable rules and regulations, thereby deceiving students as well as the government.
It was further alleged that excessive fees were being charged from students and trainees of different trades in a dishonest and fraudulent manner.
On the basis of these allegations, offences as aforesaid were registered against the petitioner and criminal law was set in motion by registration of the FIR.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute by way of compromise.

A compromise application was filed before the Trial Court and learned Trial Court by partly allowing the compromise application acquitted/discharged the petitioner/accused of the offence under Section 420 of IPC, the same being compoundable in nature.
However, the trial has continued with respect to the offence under Section 468 of IPC.

It is contended that no offence Bijesh Soni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113224513/
1 under Sections 467, 468 of IPC is made out against the petitioner as no document has been forged by him.

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that the FIR was registered on the allegation that the petitioner,
being In-charge/Principal of Radhakrishnan and Chaitanya I.T.I., collected Rs.1,000/- from students but issued receipts of only Rs.100/-.
It is urged that no act of forgery is attributable to the petitioner and, therefore, the offence under Section 468 of IPC is not attracted.

It is further submitted that only an offence under Section 420 of IPC was made out, for which the petitioner has already been acquitted on the basis of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25633 3 MCRC-18039-2017 compromise, as reflected in the order-sheet dated 10.07.2024 passed by the Trial Court, which has been placed on record.
The offences alleged are stated to be primarily of a private and economic nature, not affecting society at large.
On these grounds, it is prayed that FIR No.585/2015 and all consequential proceedings be quashed.
4. Learned counsel for the State opposes the petition.
However, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 supports the factum of compromise entered into between the parties.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
6.
The prosecution case, in nut-shell, is that the petitioner collected Rs.1,000/- from students but issued receipts for only Rs.100/-.
Upon consideration of the factual matrix, this Court is of the view that at best, offence under Section 420 of IPC is made out.
The petitioner has already been acquitted/discharged of the said offence by the Trial Court on the basis of compromise entered between the parties.

No material is available on record to prima facie establish the ingredients of the offence under Sections 467, 468 of IPC, particularly in the absence of any allegation or evidence of forgery of documents attributable to the petitioner.

7. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case as well as the material available on record, this Court finds that the dispute between the parties has been amicably resolved and the petitioner has already been discharged/acquitted of the offence under Section 420 of IPC by the Trial Court on the basis of compromise entered between the parties.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25633 4 MCRC-18039-2017 8.
So far as the offence under Sections 467, 468 of IPC are concerned, no prima facie material is available on record to establish the essential ingredients of forgery.
There is no allegation or evidence indicating that the petitioner has forged any document so as to attract the provisions of Sections 467, 468 of IPC.
Continuation of the criminal proceedings in such circumstances would amount to an abuse of the process of law.

9. Accordingly, the petition under Section 482 of CrPC, 1973 (corresponding to Section 528 of BNSS,
2023) is allowed and FIR bearing Crime No.585/2015 dated 23.09.2015 registered at Police Station Sarni, District Betul (M.P.), insofar as it relates to the offence under Sections 467, 468 of IPC, along with all consequential proceedings arising therefrom, is hereby quashed.
Certified copy as per rules.
